items.summary: पूर्वी दिल्ली के कल्याणपुरी में ड्यूटी के दौरान सफाई कर्मचारी अनिल कुमार की चाकू मारकर हत्या के मामले में पुलिस ने हत्या के आरोपी को गिरफ्तार कर लिया है. साथ ही हत्या की वजह का भी खुलासा कर दिया है. वहीं, दिल्ली नगर निगम के लिए ठेके पर काम करने वाली कंपनी मेट्रो वेस्ट हैंडलिंग प्राइवेट लिमिटेड ने मृतक के परिवार को 10 लाख रुपये का मुआवजा और एक सदस्य को नौकरी देने का आश्वासन दिया है. एमसीडी के मेयर प्रवेश वाही ने इसकी पुष्टि की है. इसके बाद बीते चार दिनों से हड़ताल पर गए कर्मचारी काम पर वापस लौट आए हैं. खोड़ा (गाजियाबाद) निवासी अनिल कुमार लगभग एक साल से मेट्रो वेस्ट कंपनी में सफाई कर्मचारी के रूप में काम कर रहे थे. 16 अगस्त, रविवार को सुबह करीब 7 बजे कल्याणपुरी के 15/16 ब्लॉक स्थित एमसीडी प्राइमरी स्कूल के पास वह कूड़ा उठाने गए थे. अनिल के साथ उनके सहयोगी गुलशन (कूड़ा गाड़ी के ड्राइवर) भी थे. इसी दौरान निहाल नाम के व्यक्ति ने अनिल पर चाकू से कई वार कर दिए. घायल अनिल को लाल बहादुर शास्त्री अस्पताल ले जाया गया, जहां इलाज के दौरान उनकी मौत हो गई. मृतक अनिल कुमार की तस्वीर. घटना के बाद मेट्रो वेस्ट हैंडलिंग प्राइवेट लिमिटेड के सफाई कर्मचारी हड़ताल पर चले गए. सफाई कर्मचारियों ने इस मामले कार्रवाई और परिवार को इंसाफ की मांग के अलावा अपनी कई मांगों को भी इस प्रदर्शन का हिस्सा बना लिया. उन्होंने मृतक अनिल कुमार के परिवार को एक करोड़ रुपये मुआवजा, परिवार के एक सदस्य को सरकारी नौकरी और आरोपी को सख्त सजा दिए जाने की मांग की. साथ ही वेतन बढ़ोतरी, सुरक्षा किट और भविष्य निधि समेत 11 मांगें रखीं. बुधवार को देर रात कर्मचारियों ने कंपनी के साथ बातचीत में सहमति बनने के बाद धरना समाप्त कर दिया. सफाई कर्मचारी जॉनी ने बताया कि उन्होंने हड़ताल इसीलिए खत्म कर दी क्योंकि कंपनी के दूसरे कर्मचारियों ने कहा कि अगर काम नहीं करेंगे तो एमसीडी टेंडर किसी और को दे देगी. ऐसे में हमेशा के लिए ही नौकरी से हाथ धोना पड़ सकता है. जिसके चलते उन्होंने काम लौटने का फैसला किया. जॉनी बताते हैं कि उनके मुद्दों पर अब 26 अगस्त को दोबारा मीटिंग होगी. कंपनी के अधिकारियों ने वादा किया है कि उनकी मांगों को सहमति बनाते हुए माना जाएगा. प्रदर्शन, हिरासत और समझौता धरने में शामिल सफाई कर्मचारी items.title: PG course in Hindi journalism discontinued at IIMC’s Amravati centre
items.summary: The Indian Institute of Mass Communication (IIMC) has discontinued its Postgraduate Diploma course in Hindi Journalism at its Amravati centre for the current academic year. This IIMC centre was established four years ago at the initiative of former President Pratibha Patil to provide professional journalism education to the youth of Vidarbha. According to a Times of India report , the institute’s Regional Director, Raj Singh Kushwaha, said the course requires a minimum of 10 students, but it did not receive sufficient admissions this time either, leading to the decision to shut it down. Kushwaha mentioned that the few students who had enrolled in the Hindi journalism course have been transferred to the institute’s Jammu centre. The institute had sanctioned 30 seats each for Hindi journalism, English journalism and Marathi journalism courses. This year, however, just 9 students enrolled for English and 10 for Marathi. After including two external students in the English journalism course, the total enrolment count for both courses stands at only 21. Meanwhile, students have alleged a lack of placement support, limited career opportunities, and a shortage of adequate faculty and facilities. They claimed that last year, even the English journalism course was taught in Hindi. Students of Marathi journalism have also complained that their employment-related expectations have not been met. Vacancies for the post of Assistant Professor are reported in the departments; however, the Director maintains that four faculty members are present, in accordance with UGC norms. Within just four years of its founding, the situation has deteriorated to the point where the Hindi course has been discontinued, and the remaining courses are running well below capacity. items.title: आईआईएमसी के अमरावती केंद्र में हिंदी पत्रकारिता का पीजी डिप्लोमा कोर्स बंद
items.summary: भारतीय जनसंचार संस्थान यानि आईआईएमसी के अमरावती केंद्र की ओर से हिंदी पत्रकारिता के स्नातकोत्तर डिप्लोमा कोर्स को इस शैक्षणिक वर्ष में बंद कर दिया गया है. टाइम्स ऑफ इंडिया की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, संस्थान के क्षेत्रीय निदेशक राज सिंह कुशवाहा ने बताया कि कोर्स चलाने के लिए न्यूनतम 10 विद्यार्थियों की आवश्यकता होती है, लेकिन इस बार भी पर्याप्त संख्या में दाखिले नहीं हुए. जिसके चलते यह फैसला लिया गया. मालूम हो कि संस्थान में यह कोर्स मात्र चार साल पहले शुरू किया गया था. कुशवाहा ने बताया कि जिन कुछ छात्रों दाखिला लिया था, उन्होंने संस्थान के जम्मू केंद्र में स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया है. गौरतलब है कि संस्थान की ओर से हिंदी पत्रकारिता के लिए 30 सीटें स्वीकृत थीं. इसी तरह अंग्रेजी और मराठी पत्रकारिता कोर्स के लिए भी 30-30 सीटें स्वीकृत थी. लेकिन अंग्रेजी में मात्र 9 और मराठी में 10 विद्यार्थियों ने ही दाखिला लिया. दो बाहरी विद्यार्थियों को शामिल करने के बाद अंग्रेजी में कुल 11 विद्यार्थी हो गए. इस प्रकार इन दोनों कोर्स में भी कुल मिलाकर 21 विद्यार्थी ही हैं. वहीं, विद्यार्थियों ने प्लेसमेंट सपोर्ट की कमी, सीमित करियर अवसर और पर्याप्त प्राध्यापकों तथा सुविधाओं के अभाव का आरोप लगाया है. उन्होंने दावा किया कि पिछले वर्ष अंग्रेजी माध्यम के कोर्स में भी हिंदी में पढ़ाई हुई. एक-एक असिस्टेंट प्रोफेसर का पद खाली बताया जा रहा है. हालांकि, निदेशक का कहना है कि यूजीसी मानदंडों के अनुसार चार फैकल्टी सदस्य मौजूद हैं. मालूम हो कि आईआईएमसी का यह केंद्र पूर्व राष्ट्रपति प्रतिभा पाटिल की पहल पर स्थापित हुआ था, ताकि विदर्भ के युवाओं को पेशेवर पत्रकारिता की शिक्षा मिल सके. लेकिन चार वर्षों में ही स्थिति ऐसी हो गई कि हिंदी कोर्स बंद हो गया और शेष कोर्स भी क्षमता से काफी कम चल रहे हैं. राज सिंह कुशवाहा का कहना है कि उन्होंने प्रचार के जरिए दाखिला बढ़ाने के प्रयास किए थे. वहीं, मराठी पत्रकारिता के विद्यार्थियों ने भी रोजगार संबंधी अपेक्षाएं पूरी न होने की शिकायत की है. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री हिंदी के 8 साल, सैकड़ों रिपोर्ट्स और एक ही वादा- सच्ची पत्रकारिता धन्यवाद मोदीजी: पत्रकारिता को 18% वाली लग्जरी कमोडिटी बनाने के लिए

items.title: Mother earning ₹1.5 lakh a month no ground to reduce father’s liability for child maintenance: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday held that a mother of a child being financially independent is not, by itself, a reason to reduce the father’s maintenance obligation towards his children. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta restored an interim maintenance award of ₹60,000 per month for two minor daughters after holding that their mother’s monthly earnings of ₹1.5 lakh could not justify halving the father’s liability. The Court said the obligation to maintain children is shared by both parents but cannot be divided through a simple mathematical calculation. “That the appellant-wife earns is not, by itself, a reason to halve the father’s liability. The obligation to maintain the children is shared by both parents, but it cannot be divided by arithmetic alone. The daughters live with the appellant-wife, who looks after their daily needs and upbringing while also working. Such care cannot be measured in money, but it is a real contribution, and often the greater one,” the Court said. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta The Court was hearing an appeal by the mother and her two daughters against an Allahabad High Court order that had reduced the father’s monthly maintenance obligation from ₹60,000 to ₹30,000, fixing it at ₹15,000 for each daughter, after taking into account that the mother was also earning ₹1.5 lakh a month. The Supreme Court found no basis for the reduction, noting that the High Court had itself accepted that ₹60,000 per month was sufficient for the two daughters having regard to the status of their parents. The Court also took into account the fact that the daughters, aged about nine and eight, lived with their mother, who was responsible for their daily needs and upbringing while also working as a gynaecologist. The Court said such caregiving constituted a contribution that could not be reduced to a monetary calculation. The Court further observed that the husband, a qualified doctor, himself claimed to earn ₹2 lakh per month. “Even if the wife’s earnings are left out of account, the reduction cannot stand. items.title: P&H High Court expresses concern over Senior Advocate's conduct after she accuses judge of bias in ex-DSP’s case
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court recently expressed concern over the conduct of a senior counsel after she accused the judge of bias for ordering an inquiry into the actions of her client without hearing her [Gursher Singh Sandhu v State of Punjab] In the order passed on August 17, Justice Sanjay Vashisth noted that Senior Advocate GK Mann , who was representing a complainant, questioned why the Court passed a direction for inquiry against her client without even hearing him. items.title: Woman serving family is homemaker irrespective of education, work status: Karnataka HC
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently held that a woman who renders services to her family is to be regarded as a homemaker irrespective of her educational qualifications or work status [Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation v Pampapal]. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha was dealing with a motor accident case of a biotechnology post-graduate, who suffered injuries in an accident involving a Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) bus. The victim, who said she had been working as a lecturer, sought enhanced compensation on account of loss of earnings due to the accident. The same had earlier been denied by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) at Bengaluru. In response, KSRTC argued that she was rightly denied compensation for loss of future earnings as there was no proof of her working status at the time of accident. It also submitted that considering her higher educational qualification, she cannot be regarded as a homemaker. However, the Court disagreed. "Every woman who renders services to her family members at home is liable to be regarded as a 'HOMEMAKER' irrespective of the fact that such woman holds higher qualification either it is a Degree or Post Graduation or a Doctorate. In the humble opinion of this Court, even a working woman or a professional can be considered to be a home maker so long as such woman renders services at home taking care and looking after the welfare of the family members," the order said. The Court added that it was not necessary in such cases to project or establish that a woman is illiterate or she stays at home 24x7 or that she attends only household work. "Any individual who tirelessly strives, showers unconditional love, sacrifices personal comfort at times and ultimately becomes a pillar for happy and stable family is a homemaker," it said. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha The Court went on to hold that the term homemaker is gender-neutral and could include a bread winner as well. "The word 'HOMEMAKER' is gender-neutral. A homemaker thus can be male or female. Also covers working person or bread winner or wage earner. Therefore this Court is of the view that the claimant in this case can well be considered to be a home maker." Considering that the accident had taken place in 2013, the Court ordered that her notional income be taken as ₹8,000 per month in absence of substantive proof with regard to her occupation. While hearing the matter, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma posed a question to the Central government counsel, "The law recognises a live-in relationship between a man and a woman. items.title: Union Cabinet approves bench at Ladakh for Jammu & Kashmir High Court
items.summary: The Union Cabinet on Thursday approved the establishment of a bench at Ladakh for High Court of Jammu and Kashmir to improve access to legal services for people living in the Union Territory. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the decision through a post made on social media platform X (formerly twitter). The Union Cabinet, under the leadership of the PM Shri @narendramodi Ji, has decided to set up a bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir in Ladakh. This will significantly enhance access to justice for citizens living in remote areas of Ladakh by reducing the time required… — Amit Shah (@AmitShah) August 20, 2026 Currently, the High Court has two benches, one at Srinagar and the other at Jammu. The Ladakh bench, once established, would be the third bench of the High Court. The home minister said the government remains committed to the development of Ladakh and to ensuring constitutional safeguards for its people. The proposed bench will be part of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, which currently serves both Union Territories. The announcement is aimed at bringing High Court services closer to litigants in Ladakh, where geographical distances can make access to judicial institutions more difficult. “This will significantly enhance access to justice for citizens living in remote areas of Ladakh by reducing the time required to avail themselves of the legal services they are entitled to,” the post read. The announcement comes against the backdrop of the continuing administrative and institutional development of Ladakh since it became a separate Union Territory in 2019 following the reorganisation of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir.

items.title: Right to marry is a human right: Madras HC suggests changes to Hindu Marriage Act to avoid obstacles to remarriage
items.summary: The right to marry is a human right and restrictions on that right must be construed strictly, the Madras High Court said while suggesting that the Hindu Marriage Act be amended to prevent a pending appeal against divorce from indefinitely holding up remarriage [Muthukumar Vs Lekha] A Division Bench of Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi said Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 should be amended to require a person challenging a divorce decree to obtain an interim stay within two months of filing the appeal. At present, Section 15 permits a divorced person to remarry only if any of the three conditions are met: where there is no right of appeal or where the time for filing an appeal has expired without one being filed or where an appeal has been filed but dismissed. This meant that a person could file an appeal against a divorce decree and keep the opposing party from remarrying. The High Court said that merely filing an appeal within time should not be enough to keep the successful spouse from remarrying for years. “ A quarter of a century has elapsed since then and we must take note of the changing social mores. We would respectfully suggest that Section 15 of the Hindu Marriage Act deserves an amendment. It should not be enough if the appeal is presented within time. The appellant must also obtain an interim stay of the decree of divorce within two months thereafter ,” the Bench said. Justices GR Swaminathan and MD Sumathi The Court was dealing with an appeal against a family court decree dissolving a marriage on the grounds of cruelty and desertion. During the pendency of the appeal, the woman remarried. Significantly, there had been no interim stay of the divorce decree. This prompted the Bench to examine the effect of Section 15 on a remarriage contracted while an appeal against the divorce decree was pending. The Court noted that although the provision speaks of remarriage becoming lawful once an appeal has been dismissed, it does not expressly state that a marriage contracted in breach of the provision is void or voidable. It referred to the Supreme Court's decision in Lila Gupta v. Laxmi Narain , which held that a marriage performed in breach of Section 15 is neither void nor voidable. items.title: Adhiraj Singh moves from MakeMyTrip to join Shaadi.com as General Counsel
items.summary: Adhiraj Singh has joined People Interactive (I) Pvt. Ltd., the company behind Shaadi.com, as General Counsel. Singh is a 2010 alumnus of National Law School of India University. With over 16 years of experience as an in-house counsel, he has held legal leadership positions across leading companies. He joins Shaadi.com from MakeMyTrip, where he most recently served as Associate General Counsel. He previously spent almost a decade at Bharti Airtel group. At Shaadi.com, Singh will lead the company's legal function, overseeing compliance, risk, and corporate legal strategy. Speaking on his new role, Singh shared, "I'm excited to join Shaadi.com at such a pivotal time for the company and look forward to helping Anupam execute his vision for the brand. I look forward to working closely with the team to support the company's growth while staying true to the trust our users place in us." Welcoming Singh on board, Anupam Mittal, Founder & CEO, People Group, said, "We're delighted to welcome Adhiraj to the People family. His experience and perspective will be a valuable addition to our leadership team as we continue to scale." items.title: Kerala HC bars lawyer from VC after he records, uploads court proceedings to his YouTube channel
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday initiated contempt of court proceedings against advocate Mathews J Nedumpara for recording court proceedings and uploading it to his YouTube channel without authorisation [ Suo motu proceedings initiated by the High Court v. Adv Mathews J Nedumpara ] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM also barred Nedumpara from appearing in any online/virtual court proceedings in Kerala until further orders. " Considering the fact that the alleged contemnor is an Advocate, we are not formally issuing a rule of contempt at this stage. However, the Department is directed to cause notice to be served on the alleged contemnor within one week from the date. The matter shall be made returnable on 7th September 2026. The alleged contemnor shall not be allowed to participate in any court proceedings in Kerala through online or virtual mode until further orders ," the order said. Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM (Kerala HC) The contempt case was initiated suo motu by the Court after its registry submitted a report stating that Nedumpara had been recording and uploading court proceedins despite repeated warnings that such unauthorised actions are violative of the Rule 3(9) of the Electronic Audio-Video Linkage Rules (Kerala), 2025. Rule 3(9) expressly prohibits broadcasting, photographing, publishing, recording or sharing of proceedings conducted under the Rules, either wholly or in part, except with the written permission of the High Court, or the concerned court of forum. The Court said that the titles under which Nedumpara had published two videos, namely “ You be the judge. Cameras can't lie. Denial of Justice to MSMEs. Watch full video on my YouTube and X ” and “ Cameras cannot lie. Denial of Justice to MSMEs. You be the judge ” also constituted criminal contempt as per Section 2(c)(i) of the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971. The Court ordered that notice of contempt proceedings be served on Nedumpara. The matter will be taken up next on September 7. "The Department is directed to circulate this order to the Hon'ble Judges of this Court and District Courts for information. This order shall be immediately intimated to the Registrar (Computerisation)–cum-Director (IT) for compliance. The Registry shall also immediately communicate this order to the alleged contemnor ," the order said. [Read Order]

items.title: RPNLUP denies irregularities in recruitment, files police complaint over defamatory press coverage
items.summary: Dr Rajendra Prasad National Law University, Prayagraj (RPNLUP) has issued a press note calling coverage of its recent Assistant Professor appointments defamatory. The press note was issued on August 20 and was signed by the University's registrar. It says that RPNLUP has filed a complaint against those responsible for the defamatory media reports. "Dr. Rajendra Prasad National Law University (RPNLUP), Prayagraj, takes serious note and unequivocally condemns, the circulation and publication of misleading, criminally intimidating, derogatory and defamatory statements, imputations and insinuations on social media and news platforms concerning the recent appointment of Assistant Professors at the University," the note reads. The note has been issued amid a State Law Department inquiry and at least two complaints. RPNLUP had advertised 12 Assistant Professor (Law) posts in March this year. Interviews for the posts were held between July 22 and 30. According to a report , the State of Uttar Pradesh's Additional Law Remembrancer, also a member of the University's Executive Council (EC), had sought records and explanations from the University's Registrar on the recruitment process. In that letter, he allegedly mentioned that complete information regarding the appointments was not placed before the EC during its meeting on July 31, because of which he and another EC member abstained from voting on the appointments. The report said that the Additional Law Remembrancer asked whether shortlisting and selection committee formation adhered to University Grants Commission (UGC) regulations, and whether an academic-score chart in the prescribed format was prepared. Separately, a complaint reportedly to the Chief Minister alleged that that three of the Vice Chancellor's (VC) former students were among those selected during the process. Another complaint, addressed to the UGC Chairman and copied to Bar & Bench , also sought a stay on one candidate's appointment and an independent inquiry, alleging the candidate's joining was permitted without the Registrar's signature. It questioned the VC's role in the process and raised fear that records may have been altered after objections were first raised. It also alleged pressure on University officials and has asked the UGC to verify the selection against academic criteria and to independently check the candidate's EWS certificate.

items.title: Bombay High Court upholds 0.25 percent IBBI regulatory fee on resolution plans under IBC
items.summary: The Bombay High Court has held that the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) possesses full statutory power to levy a 0.25 percent regulatory fee on approved resolution plans as part of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) costs [Hazel Mercantile Limited & Ors v.Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India & Ors.] A division bench of Justices Manish Pitale and Shreeram V Shirsat upheld the validity of Regulation 31A of the IBBI (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016. The provision governs the mandatory regulatory fee payable to the IBBI during CIRP. Justices Manish Pitale and Shreeram Shirsat (Bombay) The Court dismissed a batch of petitions challenging the fee as an unauthorised tax. The Bench held that the levy falls squarely within the statutory framework of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). It observed that IBBI functions as a broad regulatory authority overseeing the entire CIRP ecosystem. items.title: Plea in Supreme Court seeks CBI probe into Jharkhand Public Service Commission exam irregularities
items.summary: A plea has been moved before the Supreme Court seeking an independent Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into alleged malpractice in the Jharkhand Public Service Commission’s (JPSC) Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, 2025 [ Harisharan Devgan v. Union of India ]. The petition, filed by Advocate Satyam Singh Rajput on behalf of social activist Harisharan Devgan, seeks to transfer the ongoing investigation from the Jharkhand CID to the CBI. It argues that an agency independent of the State machinery is necessary to ensure public confidence in the outcome. The controversy stems from the JPSC preliminary examination held on April 19, 2026. After the results were declared on July 2, 2026, a carbon copy of a candidate’s OMR answer sheet went viral online which showed that he qualified despite allegedly attempting only 48 of 100 questions. This triggered allegations about how the exam had been evaluated. The Commission was already facing scrutiny over its choice of TSDPL as the examination agency, a company that had reportedly been blacklisted by the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission just months earlier over separate allegations of irregularities and confidentiality breaches. The fallout triggered sustained student protests in Ranchi, first at Bapu Vatika and later at Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium, with a student leader going on hunger strike from August 3 demanding an independent probe and structural reforms to the recruitment system. Amid the pressure, three JPSC members resigned and the State government eventually agreed to cancel the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services preliminary examination, along with backlog exams from 2023 and 2025. The government also recommended a separate Enforcement Directorate probe into alleged financial irregularities linked to the exam. However, protesting students have continued their agitation, insisting that cancelling the exams is not enough without an investigation by an agency independent of the State government. The plea assumes significance in light of a recent Jharkhand High Court decision staying the State government's decision to cancel the 2023 and 2025 exams. items.title: Supreme Court stays HC judgment mandating copyright licence for music played through cable TV in hotel rooms
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday stayed a Calcutta High Court judgment in which it was held that hotels must obtain a copyright licence before cable television facilities provided in hotel rooms can be permitted to play copyrighted music or literary works [ Hotel Appolo & Tours Pvt. Ltd. v. The Indian Performing Right Society Ltd .]. Justices KV Viswanathan and Arun Palli passed the interim order on an appeal filed by a Darjeeling-based hotel challenging the High Court's verdict. The top court issued notice in the matter and sought the response of the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS). Justices KV Viswanathan and Arun Palli By an August 4 ruling, the Calcutta High Court had ruled that hotels providing cable TV facilities in their rooms cannot avoid paying royalties for copyrighted literary and musical works merely because the cable operator has obtained a licence from the copyright holder. This judgment has now been challenged before the Supreme Court by Hotel Appolo and Tours Private Limited, which runs a hotel in Darjeeling. Its plea, filed through advocate Yashwant Singh, said that the hotel plays no music, and operates no facility where music could be played like a discotheque or a banquet hall. It has subscribed to cable television connections from a licensed cable operator and has placed a television set in each of its guest rooms, as many hotels in India do. While so, a copyright society named the Indian Performing Right Society (IPRS) sued it for copyright infringement in 2023. IPRS claimed that copyrighted literary and musical works belonging to its members were being communicated to guests through television sets installed in hotel rooms without a licence or payment of royalty. IPRS first approached the District Judge at Darjeeling in 2023 seeking to restrain the hotel from using its copyrighted works in such a manner without a licence. After the district court refused to grant it interim relief in September 2024, IPRS moved the High Court in appeal. The hotel opposed the plea, countering that it has already paid subscription charges to cable operators who held the necessary broadcast rights. Therefore, it contended that it could not be required to pay IPRS separately or compelled to secure a second copyright licence. items.summary: Congress Legislative Council member Ivan D’Souza on Thursday, August 20, strongly criticised the delay in completing the Yettinahole Integrated Drinking Water Supply Project, questioning the government over the project’s rising cost and lack of water supply to its intended beneficiaries even 12 years after its approval. Raising the issue in the Legislative Council, D’Souza said the project, approved in July 2012, was intended to divert 24.01 tmcft of water from streams flowing west of the Sakleshpur region to meet the drinking water requirements of Kolar, Chikkaballapur and other drought-hit areas. “Even after 12 years since the project began, it has not been completed. This shows the irresponsibility of the government and the officials,” he said . D’Souza pointed out that the project’s original estimated cost of Rs 8,323.50 crore had risen to Rs 12,912.36 crore in 2014 and Rs 23,251.66 crore in 2023. The estimated cost is now around Rs 30,000 crore, he said. He also criticised the absence of a clear completion deadline in the initial Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), arguing that expenditure had continued to rise without the project delivering its intended benefits. “The project cost is increasing year after year, but not a drop of water has reached its destination so far,” D’Souza said. He further questioned whether the project would be able to provide the required quantity of water, citing what he described as poor coordination among planning, land acquisition, financing, storage infrastructure and construction of the canal network. According to D’Souza, these shortcomings have resulted in substantial expenditure without the intended drinking water supply being realised. He said the government’s target of releasing water to Tumakuru by November 2026 was unlikely to be met. Responding on behalf of the Water Resources Minister, House Leader Yathindra Siddaramaiah said the project was being implemented through 54 packages. Of these, work on 20 packages had been completed, while the remaining packages were at various stages of progress. Siddaramaiah said implementation had been undertaken in phases since 2013-14 but had faced delays because of several statutory and administrative clearances, including forest, National Green Tribunal, National Highways and Railway Department approvals. items.title: How to Apply for a Credit Card With Minimal Documentation
items.summary: Getting a credit card no longer means collecting a file of papers or making repeated visits to a bank branch. Many card issuers have simplified the process, making it easier for eligible applicants to complete the formalities with only a few basic documents. The real challenge is not the paperwork but knowing what is actually required, who is eligible and how to avoid delays during the application process. A little preparation can make the experience smoother and improve the chances of approval. Before you apply for a credit card , it helps to understand what banks look for and how to keep your application complete from the beginning. Why Some Credit Card Applications Need Fewer Documents Financial institutions have simplified their verification process over the years. If your identity, address and income details can be verified through accepted records, the paperwork becomes much lighter. In many cases, the documents required depend on your employment type, income source and whether you already have a banking relationship with the credit card issuer. Applicants with updated KYC records and stable income often experience a faster application process than those with incomplete information. Key Documents Required to Apply for a Credit Card Although the exact requirements differ from one issuer to another, most applications ask for only a few common documents. These may include: ● Proof of identity such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport or Voter ID ● Proof of address if it is different from the identity document ● Income proof such as salary slips, bank statements or Income Tax Returns, depending on the card category ● Recent passport-size photograph if requested Keeping these documents ready before you apply for a credit card can help avoid unnecessary follow-ups. Who Can Apply With Minimal Documentation? Many applicants qualify for a simple documentation process if they meet the bank’s eligibility conditions. This often includes: ● Salaried individuals with regular monthly income ● Self-employed professionals with valid income records ● Existing customers of a bank with updated KYC details ● Applicants with a good repayment history Even when documentation is minimal, issuers still evaluate factors such as income, repayment capacity and credit behaviour before approving an application. items.title: Bigg Boss Agnipariksha: When queer dignity becomes prime-time entertainment
items.summary: When reality television promises an “Agnipariksha” — a literal trial by fire — it rarely acknowledges who built the furnace, who controls the thermostat, or who profits from the burn. On August 15, the premiere episode of Bigg Boss Agnipariksha Season 2 , a spin-off show designed to filter contestants for Bigg Boss Telugu Season 10 , offered a textbook demonstration of how South Indian broadcast media treats marginalised identities. Hosted by Sreemukhi, alongside a judging panel comprising actors Navdeep, Abijeet and Bindu Madhavi, the audition stage was pitched as a high-stakes arena designed to test candidates’ resilience. But when popular digital creator ‘Uppal’ Balu walked onto the stage, the interrogation that followed was not an objective assessment of his potential. It was a public execution of dignity, meticulously packaged for prime-time consumption. For years, Balu has been a ubiquitous and highly visible figure on Telugu social media. Having moved from a village to Uppal in Hyderabad, he built an online audience through flamboyant, gender-nonconforming performances, frequently wearing sarees and adopting feminine expressions. As Balu candidly explained on stage, his initial foray into content creation was rooted entirely in survival: “Many people in my family ostracised me and told me not to make videos, but I still did. Because making money was very important to me at that time. I didn’t have money for food or rent.” In a media ecosystem that offers virtually no respectable or sustainable avenues for working-class, gender-nonconforming individuals, Balu commodified the only thing algorithms and mainstream audiences demanded from him: the exaggerated performance of a caricature that cis-heteronormative viewers love to mock. He weaponised his own marginality to put food on the table, explicitly stating that he chose to live on his own terms and earn money ethically to support himself and his family. items.title: 18 yrs after eviction to build a national highway, Kochi residents still wait for justice
items.summary: “Today you can get from Kalamassery to the Kerala High Court in 20 to 30 minutes. We gave up our houses for the good of the people and I’m happy to be of service, but our sacrifice was met with violence and years of indifference,” says 69-year-old George AL. George’s family was among the 316 families evicted in 2008 for constructing National Highway 966A in Kochi. The Kerala government had carried out the eviction over nine village panchayats in order to build the four-lane highway connecting the Cochin Port to National Highway 544. However, the rehabilitation package announced has not been received in full by any of the affected people. While all the families have been allotted land on record, 192 of the allotted plots are uninhabitable. A large number of plots are allotted in marshy areas where construction is not possible. Further, none of 316 families have received a job promised to them by the Cochin Port Authority. The government also promised rent of Rs 5,000 until they move into their own homes. This promise also lapsed after two years of the evictions, despite most families being unable to move into permanent houses. Last month, the Ernakulam district administration decided to refill the marshland allotted to the evictees so that house construction can start. Eighteen years after being thrown out of their homes, this is too little too late for the evictees. A ruthless eviction The 17-km long NH 966A does not technically connect two states but has received the ‘national highway’ designation nevertheless. It connects the International Container Transshipment Terminal (ICTT) at Vallarpadam with Kalamassery on NH 544 and was built to facilitate easy transport of containers arriving at the ICTT. This was done as per a stipulation in a contract signed with Dubai Port World, the multinational shipping conglomerate that currently operates the ICTT. The contract also asked for a railway line which also led to evictions. Following the signing of this contract in 2008, hurried demolition of houses was carried out. On February 6, 2008, a large police force assembled in Moolampilly, a small island in the Kadamakkudy cluster of islands in the Periyar river. They had orders to clear the people and houses in the area. As police gathered, people who attempted to call their representatives found that MLAs and others had switched off their phones. items.title: Karnataka's New Apartment Bill explained: What changes for flat owners?
items.summary: For lakhs of apartment owners in Karnataka, a new Bill tabled in the Assembly could change who owns common areas, how maintenance is calculated, how buildings are redeveloped and how disputes within housing communities are resolved. The Karnataka Apartment (Ownership and Management) Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Assembly on Wednesday, August 19. If passed, it will replace the Karnataka Apartment Ownership Act and the Karnataka Ownership of Flats Act, both enacted more than five decades ago. The government says the existing framework has struggled to keep up with Bengaluru’s rapid expansion and the rise of large apartment projects, resulting in disputes over land, common areas, maintenance and association governance. The final Bill has also undergone changes since the draft was released in July. It now says that a fully completed apartment project can have only one registered association, even if the project was developed in multiple phases. Here is what the proposed law means for apartment owners, associations, developers and the government. Why does Karnataka need a new apartment law? The two existing laws were enacted in 1972, long before Bengaluru saw the scale of apartment development it has today. They do not adequately address issues such as ownership of common areas, transfer of land, formation of apartment associations, maintenance, financial accountability and redevelopment. The existing framework also lacks a dedicated statutory authority for apartment-related disputes. Associations have been registered under different laws, creating overlapping jurisdictions and administrative confusion. The proposed Bill seeks to bring apartment governance under one framework administered through the Urban Development Department. It would apply to projects comprising more than eight apartments, including certain villa projects. Government buildings, properties retained under single ownership and certain plotted or villa developments are excluded. Who owns the land and common areas? One of the biggest changes is the proposed legal recognition of an apartment as immovable property that can be inherited and transferred. An owner would have exclusive ownership and possession of their apartment, along with a proportionate, undivided and non-exclusive interest in the project land and common areas.
